headline: Load spike, protect today — one session, not two, and keep it honestly easy.
body_state: Readiness composite is 49.4 (red band), driven by sleep: 6.2h last night (sleep score 56), ~22h of debt over the last 14 days. HRV is still Balanced at 44ms and resting HR 49 is normal, but body battery is only 40 this morning and acute:chronic load ratio sits at 1.52 — above the 1.5 line Garmin ties to 2–4× injury risk next week. Garmin's own training-readiness score reads 69 (moderate) — that's the single-day number; the composite is pricing in this week's cumulative spike, which the daily score doesn't see. Trust the composite today.
session: Plan has two sessions stacked again today: the 5.2km Easy Run (4:35–5:03/km, RPE 3–4) and Un1t Hyrox (45min class) — the same same-day combo last week's review flagged as the ACWR driver. With today's composite red, do the easy run only and skip or move Un1t to tomorrow. Keep the run conversational — if HR climbs above ~75% max, slow down regardless of pace. If body battery hasn't climbed by afternoon, shortening the run is fine — the aerobic minutes matter more than hitting 5.2km exactly.
recent: Tue's indoor cardio (44.7min, avg HR 141, RPE 8) ran 76.7% in Zone 3/4 — grey-zone work on top of a week that's already only 16% easy against an 80% target. Monday added an Un1t class plus a 28.84km hilly bike ride (TE 1.6/0.0, still unrated so it isn't counted in load yet). Three straight days of cardio-class or unplanned volume on top of the plan — not the plan itself — is what's driving today's spike.
focus: Sleep first — ~60min earlier tonight; it's the named driver of today's red readiness, not fatigue alone.
One session today: easy run OR Un1t, not both — don't repeat Monday/Tuesday's stacking.
Rate Monday's bike ride and unplanned cardio (RPE) — they're currently invisible to your load numbers.
